summary: Serial warmups after model fallback produce p99 latency spikes and transient 504s
description: Customer reports repeated p99 latency spikes and intermittent 504s for text-generation routes after a model fallback event. The routing policy sent traffic from their pinned model to a legacy quantized variant; each incoming request appears to trigger serial warmups on replicas rather than leveraging a warm pool or shared initialization, causing amplified tail latency and occasional request timeouts.
impact: Multiple customer endpoints from LogiFlow experienced elevated p99 (2-10x baseline) for ~35 minutes during peak morning traffic. Several requests returned 504 due to request deadline exceeded. This affected user-facing features for LogiFlow's tracking UI and caused customer-reported errors and increased support load.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer has traffic pinned to redwood/gpt-7b-quantized-v1 with a fallback policy to redwood/gpt-7b-legacy-quantized.
2) Trigger a rollout or synthetic traffic spike to exceed the dedicated pool capacity, causing smart-routing to fallback to the legacy variant.
3) Observe that after fallback, multiple replicas enter initializing state and each batch of incoming requests waits for replica warmup rather than being queued behind a single initializer.
4) Monitor p99 and 504 counts at the API gateway and serving runtime for the affected route.

investigation_summary: SRE triage shows fallback to a legacy quantized variant coincided with a recent autoscaler scale-down window. Instead of using a small set of pre-warmed replicas or sharing a single initializing replica, the serving runtime created multiple replicas that performed full initialization in parallel. The legacy variant has a larger weight init time and its quantized codepath causes repeated KV cache cold misses. Requests arriving during staggered replica initializations encountered sequential warmup waits and some hit API deadline thresholds, producing 504s.
hypotheses: Autoscaler scaled down warm pool during low-traffic window; fallback happened while warm pool size was zero.
Fallback routing policy distributes traffic across multiple initializing replicas instead of funneling to a single initializer (no leader-warmup coordination).
Legacy-quantized variant performs heavier disk-to-GPU weight loads and does not reuse a shared KV cache instance, amplifying per-replica warmup time.
mitigation_actions: 1) Temporarily pin customer to original compatible variant (undo fallback) to restore latency to baseline.
2) Increase dedicated warm pool min_replicas for LogiFlow to 2 while we investigate.
3) Disable aggressive autoscaler scale-down window for the affected tenant for 48 hours.
4) Add alert for consecutive replica initializations during fallback events.
temporary_workaround: Rolled back routing for LogiFlow to their prior model version and bumped warm_pool_min to 2. This reduced p99 to near baseline within 6 minutes. Customer confirmed reduced errors in their UI.
proposed_root_cause: Combination of autoscaler-driven warm pool scale-down and fallback routing behavior that does not centralize warmup work to a single initializing replica for legacy variants with expensive weight loads.
next_steps: Engineering: Implement leader-warmup / shared-initializer behavior in smart-routing so fallback routes funnel to one initializing replica when warm_pool size is zero. (Owner: Miguel)
Runtime: Optimize legacy-quantized variant initialization path and KV cache seeding to reduce per-replica warmup time. (Owner: Priya)
SRE: Adjust autoscaler policy to respect a lower bound for warm_pool for dedicated customers with strict latency SLOs. (Owner: Sam)
Customer Success: Follow up with LogiFlow on changes and provide post-incident summary. (Owner: Leila)
Add test: end-to-end integration test that simulates fallback with warm_pool=0 and asserts single-initializer funneling.
